sources.observed_text: Lines 61-70 define a reader's end mark as the last valid commit record, unchanged for the transaction; readers use WAL pages before that mark.
sources.review_interpretation: The end-mark mechanism underlying the E04 order is already explicit in SQLite documentation. E04 operationalizes a known relation; it does not establish novelty.

sources.observed_text: Lines 10-14 define PASSIVE as checkpointing as many frames as possible without waiting and state it may leave the checkpoint unfinished when readers or writers are concurrent.
sources.review_interpretation: This documents the API behavior used by E02-E04; it does not test a lifecycle-aware policy's net benefit.

sources.retrieval: Public Crossref metadata endpoint, queried 2026-11-04 UTC; returned title 'Asynchronous and Adaptive Checkpoint for WAL-based Data Storage Systems', authors Li Zhu, Yanpeng Hu, Chundong Wang, 2023-12-17. No abstract returned.
sources.review_interpretation: A directly adjacent adaptive-checkpoint paper exists, but metadata alone cannot establish whether its method is comparable to SQLite reader lifecycle signals. Full-text comparison remains unresolved; no novelty claim is supported here.

scope: Targeted closest-work check from project-saved official SQLite pages and the E02-cited DOI. This is not a comprehensive novelty review.
